name: Liberia
snapshot: Africa's oldest republic, founded by freed American slaves, governed since 2024 by Joseph Boakai after a peaceful handover from George Weah.
culture: Liberia was founded in 1822 as a settlement for freed African Americans, whose descendants, the Americo-Liberians, dominated the country for over a century; the flag and much civic culture copy the United States. Liberian English and a love of American-style church and basketball sit alongside the traditions of the Kpelle, Bassa and other peoples, including masked secret societies.
society: Civil wars from 1989 to 2003 killed some 250,000 people, and Ebola in 2014 killed thousands more. Rubber, iron ore and gold are the main exports, and the world's largest ship registry earns fees. Most people are poor, and youth unemployment is high. A war crimes court has been approved but is yet to begin work.
situation: Joseph Boakai, a veteran politician and former vice-president, narrowly beat President George Weah, the former footballer, in 2023, and Weah conceded quickly. Boakai's government has pledged to fight corruption and to establish a court for wartime crimes, with a 2024 executive order starting the process.
power: A presidential republic modelled on the United States: the president is directly elected for six-year terms, at most two, and the legislature has a House and a Senate.
